site.name: Great Western Sugar Effluent Flume & Bridge
site.location: Kingfisher Point Natural Area, Fort Collins
overview: The Great Western Sugar Company Effluent Flume and Bridge is a surviving 1926 industrial suspension structure spanning the Cache la Poudre River in Fort Collins. It carried a metal flume that moved beet-sugar factory waste slurry across the river to settling and disposal land south of the channel.
The structure is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and survives within the City of Fort Collins' Kingfisher Point Natural Area.

timeline.text: Great Western Sugar Company built the suspension bridge and flume after its north-side settling area approached capacity, creating a route for lime-, beet-pulp-, and water-rich effluent across the Poudre River.
The Fort Collins sugar factory closed, ending the flume's industrial use.
The City of Fort Collins Natural Areas Department acquired the parcel containing the bridge and incorporated it into Kingfisher Point Natural Area.
The Great Western Sugar Company Effluent Flume and Bridge was listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its industrial and engineering significance.

moreHistory: Great Western's Fort Collins beet-sugar operation used settling ponds to separate solids from factory wastewater. When available disposal space north of the river became limited, a company engineer designed this suspension bridge to support a metal flume carrying slurry across the Cache la Poudre River.

Heritage-area interpretation identifies the slurry as largely lime, beet pulp, and water. Although most of the Fort Collins factory complex was demolished in the 1960s, the bridge and flume survived and remain visible from the Poudre Trail.

The identification point near 40.578194, -105.045139 corresponds to the documented historic structure. Visitors should use established trails and observe current City of Fort Collins Natural Areas rules rather than treating the coordinate as permission to enter or climb the structure.
